gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a screen run through a display driver (the only way to put two screens on one cable from a Mac, and the route FOPO's three-screen S788 takes on every laptop) cannot show HDCP-protected streaming video, and that on a Mac a DisplayLink driver's Screen Recording permission blocks that video on every screen, the laptop's own included (Plugable's wording, of the four pages I could open).
standout_why: I opened four of the result pages. The UPERFECT blog (cited) says only that the BE14BF's single-cable mode "does require an additional driver download" and that base M1 and M2 MacBooks support one external display. The Office Journal (rank 1) covers USB-C DisplayPort alt mode and power, with no mention of drivers, MST or HDCP. Our own triple-extender page covers one cable per screen, the Xebec MST statement and the FOPO driver, with no mention of HDCP or streaming. None of the three says what a driver-run screen cannot show. I could not read the cited Mobile Pixels Trio page (HTTP 429 on every attempt), gradedpicks.com (certificate error) or the other eight results, so this rating rests on those four pages only.
decides: It confirms the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro as the pick for two added screens under $600, with a condition: run one cable per screen from two video-capable USB-C ports. That is native video with no driver, so protected streaming is unaffected. On one cable it runs through Mobile Pixels' driver; our record's description of that driver is cut off at "a Displa…", so its identity as DisplayLink needs checking in the manual. If it is DisplayLink, Plugable's limit applies: no HDCP video on those screens, and on a Mac none on any screen while connected. The same condition applies to the UPERFECT BE14BF in single-cable mode, whose driver family I did not identify. For three added screens, the FOPO S788 through our link needs a driver on every laptop, so it should carry a caveat for shoppers who stream. The caveat is an inference: FOPO's driver is UsbDisplay, not DisplayLink, and I found no FOPO statement on HDCP. The basis is that our page has UsbDisplay using the same macOS Screen Recording permission that Plugable says disables HDCP system-wide.
